Done. The depth-pruned checkpoint is written and all checks passed on the first execution.

**What I did**

- Wrote `out/T1/solution.py`. It loads both shards via the index, drops blocks 2, 6, 10, 14, and builds a fresh dict keyed by the new names from an injective old-to-new map. Nothing is renamed in place, so a shifted block can never overwrite a survivor, and an explicit assert guards against any collision.
- Checks run before writing and again after re-reading the written file: no block index 12 or higher remains, exactly 12 q_proj tensors with contiguous indices 0..11, 7 tensors per block, 86 tensors total, and every output tensor is bit-identical in shape, dtype and values to its source under the mapping.
- The file is saved to a temp name and renamed only after verification, so a failed check leaves no output behind.
- Wrote `out/T1/REPORT.md` with the participant self-report.

**Result**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Executions | 1, succeeded |
| Output | `out/T1/model.safetensors`, 86 tensors, 12 blocks, float32, 4.0 GB |
| Run time | about 8 s |

One note on the task text: the required checks say "no tensor of blocks 12, 13, 14, 15 remains" while the removed blocks are 2, 6, 10, 14. I read that as post-renumbering indices and the script checks the output key set for any index of 12 or higher, which covers both readings.
